abstract: Báez-Duarte's "dual approximation" F_n in the Nyman–Beurling theory has as its coefficients the last row of the matrix RAMA, RAMA(n,k) = M(n/k) − M(n/(k+1)),. We describe the error of F_n exactly. In the variable y = 1/(nx) it is a 1-periodic step function whose restriction E_n to (0,1) vanishes at the reciprocals of integers, takes at rational points values that are explicit combinations of the class sums SUMMOD(q,b) of the row, jumps at a/q by −SUMMOD(q,q), tends to MERTENS(n) at 1, and satisfies the reflection formula E_n(u) + E_n((1−u)−) = MERTENS(n) + 1. In this picture the two sums that carry MERTENS(n) modulo 6 have a place: SUMMOD(6,6) is the jump of E_n at 5/6, 1 + SUMMOD(6,5) is minus its value there, and our identity 2 + SUMMOD(6,5) + MERTENS(n) = SUMMOD(6,6) is the reflection formula at u = 1/6. Secondly, we treat an endpoint case left open by Balazard and Saias for Báez-Duarte's sequence B_N: if zeta has a zero with real part exactly 1/p, then B_N does not converge in L^p(0,1); for p = 2 this is Báez-Duarte's result. Thirdly, we report an experiment with n up to one million, from an exact formula for the norm with no truncation. The norms of χ + F_n in L^p decay like a power of n for p < 2, with fitted exponents 0.24, 0.14, 0.06 at p = 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 against 0.30, 0.17, 0.07 for 1/p − 1/2, and do not decay at p = 2; two inequalities for the two sums hold at every n tested. We state three conjectures; the first answers a question of Báez-Duarte in the affirmative. All classical results are attributed. Nothing here locates a zero.
author: lasic_oblak
title: Nepo, Croats Are Breaking Through to the Centre of the R.H. Mine: Roll Up Your Sleeves
